script:
export const meta = {
  name: 'glm52-f8-f9-prefill-sweep',
  description: 'Fusions #8 and #9 gain vs prefill T, 256 to 262144, both sides retuned per point, 3 GPU lanes',
  phases: [{ title: 'Sweep', detail: '11 prefill sizes x 2 fusions across GPUs 0, 1, 3' }],
}

const COMMON = `
You are running benchmark commands for a GPU kernel-fusion study on a **MetaX C500**, then
reporting the numbers. Do NOT modify any source file, change flags, or "improve" anything.
Both scripts are smoke-tested; your job is to collect data accurately.

Environment:
- Python: /home/zhangshuhan/my-envs/fusion/bin/python
- Working dir: /home/zhangshuhan/fusion (run from here)
- **Your GPU is exclusive — prefix every command with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<N>** (your N is
  below). Two other agents benchmark on the other GPUs; touching them corrupts every timing.
  GPU 2 is hardware-dead — never use it.

This extends an existing decode sweep (T=1..1024) into the PREFILL range, T=256..262144.
Fusion #8 = MoE down-projection GEMM + expert merge. Fusion #9 = the same plus the second
residual add, reported against two unfused baselines (2-kernel and 3-kernel).

**MEMORY IS TIGHT AT THE TOP END.** T=262144 allocates ~47 GiB of the 64 GiB card (verified).
Run your commands STRICTLY SEQUENTIALLY — never two python processes at once on your GPU, or
they will OOM each other. Wait for one to write its JSON before starting the next.

Launch each with nohup and poll with a SINGLE long sleep between checks (do not chain short
sleeps):

    cd /home/zhangshuhan/fusion && CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<N> nohup \\
      /home/zhangshuhan/my-envs/fusion/bin/python -u glm52/bench/<SCRIPT> \\
      --batches <BATCHES> --tag <TAG> > /tmp/<LOGNAME>.log 2>&1 & disown

Poll until the log prints "wrote results/<f8|f9>_sweep_<TAG>.json".

Expected duration: the largest points take ~20-25 min each; your whole assignment is roughly
25-45 min. Measurement effort scales down automatically with T (a single launch is ~1.7 s at
T=262144), so do not be alarmed by low rep counts in the log at large sizes — that is by design.

Lines containing "mcErrorMemoryValueTooLarge" / "private memory" during TUNING are expected
and harmless (C500's 4 KB/thread cap rejecting candidates; the autotuner catches them). Report
them only if they appear outside tuning, or if you see a CUDA OOM.

When done, report for EVERY (script, T) in your assignment the per-point numbers the script
prints. Flag: gain spread above ~2%, rel_err above 5e-2, OOM, non-monotonic jumps, or driver
errors outside tuning.

IMPORTANT on interpretation: between-run variation on this machine is ~2.2%, roughly 20x the
within-run spread these rounds measure. Differences under ~2% are NOT resolved. Report the
numbers; do not claim trends from sub-2% wiggles.
`

const SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    lane: { type: 'string' },
    results_json: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    complete: { type: 'boolean' },
    points: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          fusion: { type: 'string' },
          T: { type: 'number' },
          fused_ms: { type: 'number' },
          unfused_ms: { type: 'number' },
          unfused3_ms: { type: 'number' },
          gain: { type: 'number' },
          gain_vs_3k: { type: 'number' },
          gain_spread_pct: { type: 'number' },
          max_rel_err: { type: 'number' },
        },
        required: ['fusion', 'T', 'gain'],
      },
    },
    anomalies: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['lane', 'results_json', 'complete', 'points'],
}

const LANES = [
  { gpu: 0, lane: 'lane0',
    cmds: [['bench_f8_sweep.py', '262144', 'prefill_lane0'],
           ['bench_f9_sweep.py', '262144', 'prefill_lane0']] },
  { gpu: 1, lane: 'lane1',
    cmds: [['bench_f8_sweep.py', '131072,65536,32768', 'prefill_lane1'],
           ['bench_f9_sweep.py', '131072', 'prefill_lane1']] },
  { gpu: 3, lane: 'lane2',
    cmds: [['bench_f9_sweep.py', '65536,32768,16384,8192,4096,2048,1024,512,256', 'prefill_lane2'],
           ['bench_f8_sweep.py', '16384,8192,4096,2048,1024,512,256', 'prefill_lane2']] },
]

phase('Sweep')
log('Prefill sweep 256..262144 for #8 and #9 across GPUs 0/1/3 (T=262144 uses ~47 GiB — run serially)')

const out = await parallel(
  LANES.map((l) => () =>
    agent(
      COMMON +
        `\n# YOUR ASSIGNMENT\nGPU: **CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=${l.gpu}**\n` +
        `Run these commands ONE AT A TIME, in this order:\n` +
        l.cmds
          .map((c, i) =>
            `  ${i + 1}. script=${c[0]}  --batches ${c[1]}  --tag ${c[2]}` +
            `   (log /tmp/${c[0].includes('f8') ? 'pf8' : 'pf9'}_${l.lane}.log,` +
            ` output results/${c[0].includes('f8') ? 'f8' : 'f9'}_sweep_${c[2]}.json)`)
          .join('\n') +
        `\n\nReport every point from both runs.\n`,
      { label: `prefill-${l.lane}-gpu${l.gpu}`, phase: 'Sweep', schema: SCHEMA }
    )
  )
)

return { lanes: out.filter(Boolean) }

lanes.anomalies: No flaggable anomalies. Gain spreads 0.056% (f8) and 0.083% (f9), far under the ~2% flag threshold; rel_err max 1.02e-2, under 5e-2; zero OOM; zero CUDA/driver errors outside tuning. All 5 (f8) and 6 (f9) mcErrorMemoryValueTooLarge / "private memory 4 KB/thread cap" messages fall strictly between [cfgs] tuning lines (verified by log line number and timestamp) — expected autotuner candidate rejections. Monotonicity not assessable within this lane: only one T point (262144) was assigned; cross-lane monotonicity must be checked by the orchestrator against lanes 1/2. Runs were strictly sequential on GPU 0 (f8 PID 1641390 confirmed exited and GPU memory back to 1.2 GiB before f9 PID 1709169 launched); peak memory 46.6 GiB (f8) and 49.4 GiB (f9) of 65.5 GiB. OBSERVATION, not an anomaly: at T=262144 both fusions are net LOSSES — fused is ~15% SLOWER than unfused (f8 0.8534x; f9 0.8520x vs 2-kernel, 0.8608x vs 3-kernel). This is ~14-15% away from parity, i.e. ~6-7x the stated ~2.2% between-run variation, so the sign of the effect is well resolved even though the exact magnitude carries that ~2.2% uncertainty. The f9 vs-2k and vs-3k gains differ by ~1.0%, which is BELOW the ~2.2% between-run resolution — do not read the 2k/3k baseline ordering as resolved. Tuned configs converged to the same tile for both sides (BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_K=32, num_warps=16, num_stages=3; GROUP_M 4 unfused vs 16 fused), and the f9 seed step selected the torch impl (4.4856 ms) over triton (10.0037 ms).

None to flag. All four points are clean against every stated criterion.

- Gain spread: max 0.227% (F8 T=32768); all well under the ~2% threshold.
- rel_err: max 1.06e-2 (F8 T=32768 fused side); all well under 5e-2.
- OOM: none. Peak observed device memory was 26.2 GiB (F8) / 27.7 GiB (F9) of 64 GiB. GPU 1 returned to its 858 MiB idle baseline after each run.
- Driver errors: "mcErrorMemoryValueTooLarge" / "private memory ... 4 KB/Thread, kernel request 5-6 KB/thread" lines appeared ONLY during autotuning in both logs, each immediately followed by a successful "[cfgs] ..." selection line. Zero occurrences of OOM, Traceback, or CUDA error anywhere in either log (grep count 0 in both).
- Monotonicity: F8 gain moves smoothly with T (0.9014 -> 0.8798 -> 0.8565 as T goes 32768 -> 65536 -> 131072); both unfused and fused times scale ~1.88-1.97x per doubling of T. No jumps.

Cross-run consistency check (informational, not a flag): at T=131072 the F8 and F9 numbers agree closely -- F8 unfused 375.62 vs F9 2-kernel baseline 376.38 (0.20% apart), F8 fused 438.67 vs F9 fused 439.88 (0.28% apart). Both differences are far inside the ~2.2% between-run variation on this machine.

Interpretation caveat honored: every fusion here is a SLOWDOWN (gain < 1.0 at all four points, i.e. fused is 11-17% slower than unfused), and those margins are large enough to be real. But the F9 gap between the 2-kernel (0.8555x) and 3-kernel (0.8646x) baselines is ~1.1%, which is below the ~2% resolution floor -- I am not claiming a difference between those two baselines. Likewise, no trend claim is made from any sub-2% wiggle.

Both runs executed strictly sequentially; the f8 process was confirmed exited and GPU 1 back to idle before f9 was launched. No source files, flags, or configs were modified.

Runtime: f8 sweep 05:07-05:56 UTC (~49 min), f9 sweep 05:57-06:17 UTC (~20 min).

INCOMPLETE — no data collected yet. I was required to return structured output before the benchmarks finished, so this report contains zero measured points and must not be treated as results.

Status at time of reporting:
- Run 1 (bench_f9_sweep.py --batches 65536,32768,16384,8192,4096,2048,1024,512,256 --tag prefill_lane2) is STILL RUNNING on CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=3, PID 1641591, log /tmp/pf9_lane2.log. It had printed only "allocating w2 = 6.0 GiB" and the header "--- T=65536 rows=524288 (2048.0/expert) [tune 2/6, measure 4/10] ---". It is in the autotuning phase of the FIRST of nine points; no per-point result line has been emitted. results/f9_sweep_prefill_lane2.json does not exist.
- Run 2 (bench_f8_sweep.py --batches 16384,8192,4096,2048,1024,512,256 --tag prefill_lane2) has NOT been started. It must not be started until run 1 writes its JSON, per the strict-sequential memory constraint.
- A background waiter (bash task b2xwbak5y) is armed and will fire when /tmp/pf9_lane2.log contains "wrote results/f9_sweep_prefill_lane2.json" or the python process exits.

Anomalies observed so far: NONE. No OOM, no CUDA errors, no mcErrorMemoryValueTooLarge / private-memory lines at all yet (log is 3 lines). GPU 3 was idle and healthy at launch (mx-smi: 858/65536 MiB used, 49C, Available). Other lanes' processes (bench_f8_sweep prefill_lane0 on T=262144, prefill_lane1 on 131072,65536,32768) are running as expected on other GPUs and were not touched; GPU 2 was not used.

To finish the assignment, this subagent needs to be re-invoked (or allowed to continue) so it can: wait for run 1 to write results/f9_sweep_prefill_lane2.json, then launch run 2, then report all 9 f9 points (fused_ms, unfused2_ms, unfused3_ms, gain_vs_2k, gain_vs_3k, gain_spread_pct, rel_err) and all 7 f8 points.
